Not level 20 (Isolated): that needs exactly 2 satisfied indicators, and no second indicator could be satisfied. A5 is awarded, and deliberately so: the rubric's A5 admits a first-party shipped component, and quidra-lang/dnn is a released, installable package whose official repository states it is written in ordinary Quidra source code; marking it down would be scoring Quidra below what the observable criterion says. uniform_admissibility_rules_applied_to_a: A1-A3 organization count: an organization is counted only when a publicly retrievable, DATED, organization-published artefact states that a component the organization ships is implemented in the language. Two artefact classes were admitted, identically for all ten: (i) an official first-party case-study/user page published by the language's own project, and (ii) the official repository (description or README) of a product/component owned by the adopting organization.

Dating rule: for (i) the dated items on the page; for (ii) the repository's pushed_at timestamp when the excerpt comes from the repository description, and the last commit date of the README file when the excerpt comes from the README. Every excerpt is verbatim and at most 15 words, per the metric's anti_fabrication_rule.

Organizations belonging to a language's own frozen official_project_set were excluded from that language's A1-A3 count (Apple for Swift; Microsoft, npm and Node.js/OpenJS for TypeScript; JetBrains for Kotlin; quidra-lang for Quidra; the Go project, rust-lang, PSF/CPython, WG21+LLVM+Apple, OpenJDK+Oracle, ZSF for the others).

A6 used one single source for all ten languages - the 2025 Stack Overflow Developer Survey, 'Programming, scripting, and markup languages', All Respondents tab - so that the same population instrument is applied to every language; the TIOBE index was used only as a secondary check for Quidra.
Absence of evidence was never treated as satisfaction, for any language, including for Bun and TigerBeetle under Zig.
cross_language_consistency_note: The same six indicators were scored from the same two evidence classes, in the frozen evidence_collection_order with Quidra last, so no threshold was settled after seeing Quidra. Every language was searched for a first-party case-study/user page (found for Go and Kotlin; absent for Python's dated pages, C++, Rust - the old rust-lang.org production-users page 404s at the cutoff - Java, TypeScript, Swift, Zig and Quidra), and every language was then searched through organization-owned official repositories with the identical procedure and the identical accept/reject test. Eight languages reached 20+ distinct organizations and satisfied all six indicators, so they share level 100 - the rubric is a six-indicator checklist that mature ecosystems all pass, and no interpolation between levels is permitted. Zig failed A3 alone and sits one level lower at 80. Quidra satisfies A5 only and sits at 0. The level boundaries were checked in both directions afterwards: no two languages with the same observable evidence received different levels (all eight 100s satisfy the identical six indicators), and no two with clearly different evidence received the same level (Zig's 5 verified organizations vs. the 21-26 of the languages above it; Quidra's 0 vs. Zig's 5).
limitations: No Microsoft-published governance document specific to TypeScript was located; TypeScript's A4 governance conjunct rests on the Node.js/OpenJS project, which the frozen official_project_table lists as official for TypeScript. If a reviewer rejects that, TypeScript's A4 fails and its level drops to 80.

python.org/about/quotes/ and the go.dev and kotlinlang.org case-study index pages carry no explicit publication date; the Go and Kotlin pages were counted for A3 under the uniform dating rule (dated items on the page), while python.org/about/quotes/ was recorded as supporting evidence only and Python's A3 rests entirely on 21 individually dated repository citations.

Bun and TigerBeetle are widely described as Zig codebases but neither repository's description nor README contained a retrievable implementation-language statement at the accession time, so they were excluded from Zig's count. Including both would still leave Zig at 7, far short of A3's 20.

GitHub public code search for Quidra source files returned zero results; GitHub code search does not index every repository, so this is evidence of absence at the search level rather than proof that no private or unindexed Quidra use exists. A1 is failed on lack of positive evidence, which is the rule applied to all ten.

The organization counts are lower bounds, not censuses: verification stopped once the 20-organization threshold was passed, so the tables under-report Python, C++, Rust, Go, Java, TypeScript, Kotlin and Swift. This cannot change any awarded level, since A3 is a threshold.

All web accessions occurred between 2026-09-19T00:25Z and 2026-09-19T01:10Z on the benchmark host; per-entry timestamps inside that window are recorded to the minute for page fetches and to the second for the Stack Overflow survey and the GitHub API calls.
